author: Linnaeus, 1758
habitat: 강어귀, 바닷가, 먼바다, 작은 연못, 논, 습지
summary: 봄과 가을에 우리나라를 지나가는 나그네새로, 강어귀와 바닷가, 먼바다에서 지내고 작은 연못이나 논, 습지에서도 산다. 크고 작은 떼를 지어 다니며 물속에 사는 곤충, 연체동물, 갑각류 등을 주로 먹는다. 알은 한배에 4~7개를 낳으며, 국내에서는 성진, 만포 등지를 거쳐 간다.

points.en: blackish-slate lower back, rump and uppertail coverts fringed white

sexes.female: 여름깃은 등이 어두운 석판색이고 윗등에 모래빛 살구색 세로무늬가 있으며, 아래등·허리·위꼬리덮깃은 검은 석판색에 가장자리가 희다.

art.subject: Red-necked Phalarope (Phalaropus lobatus), adult female in breeding plumage as seen on Korean coastal waters in May: head and hindneck dark slate-grey with a small white spot above the eye; chin and throat white; a bright chestnut-orange band runs from behind the eye down the side of the neck and across the foreneck; breast-sides and flanks slate-grey, rest of the underparts white; mantle and scapulars dark slate with bold sandy-buff stripes along their edges; lower back, rump and uppertail coverts blackish-slate fringed white. Bill black, needle-thin; dark eye; legs dark grey with lobed toes.
art.pose: swimming on calm water, side view
art.scene: Korean estuary during spring migration in May, calm open water near the shore; no people, buildings or text
views: adult female breeding plumage (May), side view swimming: dark slate head with a small white spot above the eye, white throat, chestnut-orange neck band, slate breast-sides, dark slate back with sandy-buff stripes, needle-thin black bill
adult male breeding plumage (May), side view swimming: same pattern but duller and browner, the neck band paler orange-buff and less extensive, more white above the eye

adult winter plumage (autumn and winter), side view swimming: white forehead and underparts, dark rear crown, black patch through and behind the eye, pale grey upperparts with white feather edges forming pale stripes on the back
in flight seen from above: dark wings with a clear white wing-bar, sandy-buff back stripes, blackish-slate rump fringed white, white sides to the rump and tail base
art.build: Small, dainty wader, about 18cm, a little larger than a sparrow, that usually swims, floating high and buoyantly like a tiny gull and often spinning on the spot to stir up food. Small round head, slender neck. Bill black, straight and needle-thin, about as long as the head. Legs short, dark grey, with lobed toes. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip or a little beyond. In flight a clear white wing-bar on dark wings and a dark centre to the rump and tail with white sides.
avoid: Do not paint a thick bill or a yellow bill base — Red Phalarope has a thicker, yellow-based bill; this one is black and needle-thin.
Do not paint the male brighter than the female; in phalaropes the female is the more colourful sex.
Do not show the chestnut neck on winter birds; they are grey and white with a black eye-patch.
Do not paint it wading on long legs; it usually swims, sitting high on the water.
